title: harper-cole-private-deploy-scratchpad-2026-03-06
content:
Quick daily scratchpad for current private deploy work (notes to self, checklist, customer blockers).

Context:
- Onsite-ish install for Customer X (air-gapped, VPC + on-prem gateway).
- Goal: get private control plane + serving runtime up in their VPC with KMS integration and GPU nodes.
- Contact: Lina (Customer X infra) — linab@example.com.
- Ticket: PD-3147 (net/proxy + registry mirror).

Top-of-mind TODOs (prioritized):
1) Finalize image mirror plan with customer (registry credentials + scope) — blocking step for air-gapped install.
2) Confirm KMS/HSM integration details (key wrapping flow, CSR + cert timeline).
3) Validate GPU node firmware + driver baseline (list required versions in ticket).
4) Prep offline bundle (images, helm charts, k8s CRDs) and test in local air-gapped VM.
5) Update runbook with customer-specific firewall rules and DNS entries.

Install checklist (working, not exhaustive):
- Precheck: collect hardware inventory & network map (done? ask Lina for vSwitch diagram).
- Network:
  - Ensure L3 connectivity between control-plane nodes and worker nodes.
  - Required outbound endpoints (if not allowed, prepare registry mirror + certs): registry.redwood-internal.example, time.redwood.example (for NTP fallback).
  - Ports: 6443, 2379-2380, 10250, 30000-32767 (nodePort range) + custom 8443 for control-plane ingress. Confirm customer firewall ACLs.
  - MTU: customer uses jumbo frames (9000). Need to confirm kube CNI MTU override.
- DNS:
  - Add control-plane FQDNs to customer internal DNS.
  - Control-plane cert CN must match internal FQDNs.
- Security:
  - KMS: They use AWS CloudHSM in their VPC (private). Need IAM role mapping and IP allowlist.
  - SSH bastion for initial debugging only. Ensure keys rotate after install.
- OS / Kernel:
  - RHEL 8.6 baseline (customer uses RHEL). Disable firewall only if they want kube-proxy iptables mode; prefer opening ports instead.
  - sysctl: net.ipv4.ip_forward=1, vm.max_map_count=262144 (if using ES for logs), fs.file-max >= 100000.
- GPU stack:
  - NVIDIA driver: >= 535.x required.
  - CUDA: 12.1 recommended for our runtime.
  - Validate nvidia-container-runtime and containerd config (systemd cgroup driver).
  - Test commands: nvidia-smi, nvidia-smi topo --matrix, dmesg | grep NVRM.
- Container runtime / k8s:
  - containerd 1.7.x recommended. Configure proxy env for image pulls if needed.
  - Kubernetes 1.26 tested with our runtime. Confirm their OS kernel compatibility.
  - Helm 3.10+ for our charts.
- Storage:
  - PVCs for model cache (fast NVMe recommended). If they have no dynamic provisioner, use pre-provisioned PVs.
- TLS / Certs:
  - Provide CSR process for control-plane certs. We can generate CSR for them to sign if required.
- Logging / Metrics:
  - Fluentd -> centralized log collector (they have Splunk). Need output config.

Air-gap specifics / registry mirror notes:
- Mirror strategy: pull images from our hosted registry into customer private registry (harbor). Provide script + tarball with images and signed manifests.
- Auth: they prefer short-lived tokens. Need service account and an admin user on their registry. Blocker until registry admin provides creds.
- Image digest pinning: recommend pinning digests in helm values to avoid mutable tags.

Known customer blockers right now:
- Network team requires ticket for opening outbound to our artifact host (they call it "external-entitlement"). PD-3147 is open but waiting on approval.
- HSM team needs compliance doc on keykeeping (we have template but must populate with customer-specific network CIDRs).
- Ops: they use a transparent proxy that breaks TLS SNI for some registry traffic — need an explicit exception or use mirror through internal registry.

Troubleshooting cheat-sheet (commands I use frequently):
- Check k8s nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node <node>
- Pod logs: kubectl -n redwood-system logs deploy/runtime-controller
- Verify images present on node: crictl images | grep redwood
- Containerd pull with proxy: ctr --namespace k8s.io images pull --user <user>:<pw> <registry>/<image>@<digest>
- GPU: nvidia-smi; nvidia-smi topo --matrix; dmesg | tail -n 80
- Network trace: curl -v --resolve control.redwood.internal:8443:<IP> https://control.redwood.internal:8443/healthz

Notes / fragments to clean into runbook later:
- Add step: pre-seed /etc/hosts with control-plane FQDNs for initial bootstrap (customer DNS often lags).
- Consider providing small k3s-based test bundle for customers who want lightweight PoC before full k8s install.
- Add explicit checklist item: check LCM (lifecycle manager) version compatibility with our operator.

Meeting follow-ups (today):
- 10:30 sync w/ Lina — confirm registry admin contact and get CIDRs for HSM (action: Riley to loop in).
- 14:00 runbook review w/ Samira — go over firewall rules and cert flow.

Random todo / notes to self:
- Pack offline bundle on my laptop (steps documented in Confluence). Bring USB thumb drive (encrypted).
- Prepare quick "what we need from you" one-pager for customer (ports, DNS entries, registry access, KMS key policy).
- Add pointer in runbook: how to rotate KMS keys and update control-plane (one-liner + backup steps).

End of scratchpad.

-- Harper
